The story presents holding the cast and fingers between sunlight and the film as a test of X-ray absorption, saying the fingers only block some. That is visible light, which a hand blocks almost completely, so it shows nothing about X-rays. The fact itself is correct (checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiography).

Liam's line is said to sit under Vihaan's on a shared distance-time graph, yet it is called steeper and faster. A line lying below another one from the same start is the less steep, slower one.

The story sets the metronome weight near the bottom of the pendulum and gets a slow tick. Moving the weight down toward the pivot makes the tempo faster, and the pendulum stands upright rather than hanging (checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metronome). The Maelzel 1815 fact is correct.

The story says a quarterback who throws one touchdown pass does not get a 158.3 rating. Under the capped formula, a 1-for-1 touchdown pass of 12.5 yards or more scores exactly 158.3 (checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passer_rating).
Arithmetic redone: 10.60, 11.24, 13.38 vs 13.00; 72/6=12, 72/12=6. Checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_72.

The story quotes the line as 'But soft, behold what light through yonder window breaks?' Shakespeare wrote 'But soft, what light through yonder window breaks?' with no 'behold' (checked: gutenberg.org/files/1513). The thee/thou fact is correct (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thou).
Arithmetic redone: 5x+4=24 gives x=4, and 24/9 fails the check.
A father letting a child ride in the cargo area of a moving truck among loose boxes is shown as fine. That is unsafe and illegal in many places.

The story reads a pH of about 2 off a litmus strip using a pH chart. Litmus only shows acid or base; its colour change happens over roughly pH 4.5 to 8.3, so it cannot give a pH value (checked: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litmus).

The story gives the 1996 averages as Justice .311 and Jeter .314, which makes Jeter the 1996 winner. In fact Justice hit .321 and Jeter .314, so Justice led in both years.
